survey: The object is a puffy cream envelope seen almost straight on, with a slight downward view. The open back flap rises behind the top edge and shows its inner face, which fits a camera a little above the envelope. Three photos sit upright inside the envelope and fan slightly to the right. The front photo is tilted a few degrees and its lower part is hidden behind the V-shaped front pocket, so it plainly sits inside the envelope. The pocket's diagonal folds meet at a point near the center, and both sides look the same, as they should on a face-on front. The pink house stamp and the round postmark with wavy lines lie flat on the front face. Because that face points straight at the camera, the stamp is a near-rectangle and the postmark is a near-circle, which is correct. The scene printed on the photo has its own perspective and doesn't need to match the envelope. The envelope floats with no ground under it, so there is no contact to check. Every part agrees on one slightly-above, front-on view.
